ticket: TypedArray regression fix (blocking origin/dev push, ahead of JSRT-16)

root_causes.iter-prototype (6 files): binary_typed_iterator in builtins_binary.rs set the TypedArray iterator's [[Prototype]] to Object.prototype instead of the shared %ArrayIteratorPrototype% that CreateArrayIterator uses for both Array and TypedArray iterators. Fixed by reusing std_sequence_iterator_proto(SequenceIteratorKind::ArrayValues), the same prototype Array.prototype.values/keys/entries already share.
root_causes.from/custom-ctor-returns-smaller-instanc: binary_construct_typed_object (shared by %TypedArray%.from and .of) never checked that a constructor returned an instance at least as long as requested; %TypedArray%.of already had its own redundant check after the call, but .from had none and silently dropped tail elements. Moved the length check into binary_construct_typed_object itself so every caller gets it.
root_causes.indexOf/coerced-searchelement-fromindex-: includes/indexOf/lastIndexOf re-read values/length from the view AFTER coercing fromIndex, so a fromIndex valueOf that grows a resizable ArrayBuffer let the search see the newly grown region. The spec reads TypedArrayLength once, before fromIndex coercion, and searches that fixed window regardless of a later resize. Fixed by using the values/length already captured at the top of binary_typed_method (pre-coercion) instead of re-reading post-coercion.
root_causes.with/ignores-species and with/negative-i: with() resolved a negative index against the CURRENT (post-value-coercion) length instead of the length captured before any coercion, and used @@species for the result contrary to the current spec text (which always uses the intrinsic constructor for the TypedArray's own kind, ignoring species). Fixed the negative-index base and replaced binary_typed_species_from_values with binary_typed_from_values.

verification.method: Full unsharded Test262 run (not sharded/Boat) directly via scripts/linux-run.sh js-runtime --ref <sha>, to avoid a shard-reuse staleness bug observed in scripts/test262-boat.sh (a Boat sandbox served a stale shard.json from a prior run after its own remote command exited nonzero; the merge step did not detect this because it only checks the file is non-empty). Diffed the resulting records array against .agents/test262/baseline.json directly.

typedarray_subtree_vs_baseline.note: The only TypedArray-tree loss is a timeout on a pre-existing SpiderMonkey stress test unrelated to this diff (no TypedArray/Proxy exotic-object code was touched that this test exercises); timeouts are an explicitly allowed loss category per the coordinator's instruction. All 11 originally-reported regressions plus their pairs now pass, confirmed individually and as part of this full run.

non_typedarray_losses.assessment: None touch amazing-js code this fix or JSRT-15 changed (destructuring rest patterns, async-arrow-function, intl402, async generator methods). Very likely pre-existing drift between the Sep-26 19:44 baseline.json and the current dev tip (which has absorbed many unrelated lane merges since), not something this commit introduced. Not fixed here: out of this ticket's TypedArray scope; flagged in questions.md for the integrator to consider refreshing baseline.json.
